review_method: Actual raw generation images, eight original guides plus one repair guide, per-pose registered original/candidate comparison contacts, then all fifteen source-ordered group contacts and decoded source/mirror GIF frame strips in fifteen review boards. Static images were viewed; no timed animation playback is asserted.
review_scales: Raw pages and single repair were inspected enlarged. Registered comparison files retain projected original/candidate pixels at 1:1 within panels; the tool may downsample the whole contact for display. Group review boards are reduced overviews for order/entry/exit/repeat/facing checks, not fine-pixel anatomical proof.

review_sets.observations: Viewed raw batch-000-a, original guide and registered 1:1 comparison; walked source pose order shows changing feet and low carried hammer, with free/secondary hand placement visible. Full hammer and both feet remain inside the registered frame. Generated master anatomy is broader than OG and aspect-fit can reduce visible height; no scaling override applied.

Viewed raw batch-001-a, original guide and registered comparison; walk return and idle gesture keep source facing, bare foot/boot and progressively lowered hammer. Candidate rendering differs in proportions from OG. No extra limbs, missing equipment or clipping observed at inspected scales.

Repair: original batch-001-a p015 hammer was too vertical. Viewed single-pose source guide, newly generated repair-p015-b and registered comparison. The replacement restores the diagonal down-right shaft and corresponding grip/free hand; full feet and cross-head fit. Retained the old attempt/history and rebuilt G2.

Viewed raw batch-002-a and registered OG comparison for every pose. Quiet idle variants lead into forward crouch, arms-up recoil, backward lean, sideways lean and recovery. Hammer, bent legs, bare foot/boot and raised/free arm transitions are visible without added limbs or frame clipping.

Viewed raw batch-003-a and registered OG comparisons. Two-hand defence lifts from low horizontal through diagonal/vertical guard then lowers. Death recoil then lifts the booted knee with spread arms. Hammer head/shaft and hands stay attached and visible.

Viewed raw batch-004-a and all registered OG comparisons. Death sequence folds to a low corpse, preserving the boot and bare foot with hammer across/above the folded body; no extra detached limbs observed. Turn changes from three-quarter toward frontal view and vertical hammer, not a fabricated back view. Native low corpse bounds retained by registration.

Viewed raw batch-005-a and registered OG comparison for each pose. Upper windup, behind-head hammer, raised strike and lowering recovery remain distinct from front-attack preparation. Two-hand grip during lifted actions and one-hand recovery are visible; complete hammer/feet retained.

Viewed raw batch-006-a and registered OG comparison for each pose. Front attack extends horizontally, recovers diagonally, then low attack winds overhead and folds forward toward ground. Hand grips, hammer head angle and both feet remain present; no missing limbs or clipped artwork observed.

Viewed raw batch-007-a and registered OG comparisons. Low-attack recovery rises toward separate movement-start/end source poses. Distinct foot/torso/hammer drawings remain separate IDs; full weapon and feet fit. No idle substitution was used.

quality_limits: Independent high-resolution drawings are not pixel-identical silhouettes; body proportions, cloth folds and texture vary slightly. The required source-bound aspect-fit can reduce visible height where the high-resolution silhouette is broader. No independent pose/weapon/body scaling was introduced.
Static overview review establishes inspected pose/order/facing observations, not smoothness, subjective animation acceptance, subpixel edge perfection or original timing.
No browser, Godot, engine import, gameplay, human playback or final motion approval was performed.
